title: Notes two chords share
summary: A note in both chords can simply stay where it is.

steps.title: Common tone
steps.body:
C major (C E G) and A minor (A C E) share C and E. A note that is in both chords is a **common tone**. When you change chords, keep the common tones held and move only the rest.

**Why it matters:** Holding common tones is the simplest voice-leading trick there is. It makes chord changes smooth with almost no effort.

steps.title: C and G share G
steps.body: C E G and G B D have one common tone: G.

items.prompt: Which note do C and G share?
Play C, E and G, then keep C held and play the chord written F/C.

steps.title: Hold and move
steps.body: Play C, Am, F and G in turn. Before each change, find the common tones and keep those fingers down.

items.prompt: Which note do C and F share?
